verdict: HOP ACCOUNTABILITY (hop_accountability.py): the user's correction -- a hop only carries causation if the intermediate ACTUALLY CHANGED the required way, not merely 'was reachable'. Auditing every hop's measured abundance change AND direction. GATA1 detail: of 233 specific movers, only 5 (2%) have a shortest chain that is fully confirmed; the rest break, 137 of them at a SILENT intermediate that didn't change at all (e.g. GATA1==represses==>MYC but MYC's mRNA is flat, so GATA1->MYC->LTB never actually fired). Allowing ANY confirmed path, operative reach is 27/233 (12%), +3.2sigma above the sign-flip null -- so the confirmed agreement that exists is real, but small. THE HEADLINE is the aggregate direct-target audit (396 unique signed KO->target pairs): only 3% of a knockout's OWN annotated direct targets even change (|z|>=1) -- 97% are transcriptionally SILENT in the KO -- and of the few that move, only 17% go the annotated activation/repression direction; 83% go the OPPOSITE way (in K562 the wiring's SIGN has flipped vs the database -- e.g. GATA1's curated 'activation' targets rise when GATA1 is removed, because in this context GATA1 represses that myeloid program). So 'the protein that was supposed to work one way' mostly (a) doesn't respond, or (b) responds the other way. Operative chains reach just 0.2% of specific movers (2.6x the null), and co-movement supports coupling only weakly (3.1x). MEANING: the hop critique is decisive -- demanding that each intermediate's state actually changed as required dissolves almost all the 'named' chains from case_study; what survives is a small, direction-confirmed core. The knockout-specific response is not a traceable cascade of confirmed state-changes through the curated wiring -- most of that wiring is silent or sign-flipped here. This is an ABUNDANCE audit; silent intermediates could still act through activity/PTM mRNA cannot see -- exactly the unmeasured layer the ceiling lives in. Deterministic; GATA1 detailed + all scorable KOs.
